title: Methods for identifying the material-recyclable share of SRF during co-processing in the cement industry
author: Aldrian, Viczek, et al.
materials: Researched data based on literature references do not permit adequate estimations of the relative amount in SRF that would be attributable to recycling. First, Tables 1 and 2 clearly show that only few data from the references are available for both the ash content and the composition of SRF ashes. Second, quality and reliability of data are insufficient for all parameters due to the large differences between values given in the literature. Furthermore, different incineration temperatures used in determining the ash content (550 °C and 815 °C) and different methods (XRF, ICP-OES) for analysing the ash have been used in the references examined (cf. Tables 1 and 2), preventing direct compatibility of data.

Method A: For measurements using X-ray fluorescence analysis (XRF), fused beads were made out of SRF samples incinerated at 950 °C. In each case, 1 g of sample was thoroughly mixed with 8 g of di-lithium tetraborate (Li2B4O7, Sigma Aldrich) and melted in a platinum crucible (HD Elektronik und Elektrotechnik GmbH, Fusion Machine Type VAA2). The fused bead was then measured using XRF (PANalytical, Axios). The software GeoWSU was used for quantitative evaluation. This procedure is pursuant to Section 10.3 of EN 15410 [38]. Examinations were carried out in duplicate.
All experimental tests were carried out once.

steps.title: Collect and select SRF samples
steps.instruction: Obtain the 80 SRF samples supplied by manufacturers and cement plants (50 primary, 30 secondary) from Austria, Slovenia, Croatia and Slovakia; randomly select the subset required for each analytical test.

steps.title: Dry and grind samples
steps.instruction: Dry each original SRF sample in a drying oven at 105 °C until constant mass, then grind to particle size <0.5 mm using a Fritsch Pulverisette 18 cutting mill with cyclone (EN 15413). Re‑dry the ground material at 105 °C before any incineration or melting step.

steps.title: Incinerate for ash preparation
steps.instruction: Place the dried, <0.5 mm material in a muffle furnace (Nabertherm L 9) and incinerate at 950 °C ± 25 °C for 2 h (EN 196‑2) to obtain ash for Methods A, B and D. Keep the incinerated residue in a desiccator before further processing.

steps.title: Prepare fused bead for XRF (Method A)
steps.instruction: Weigh 1 g of the incinerated ash, mix thoroughly with 8 g of di‑lithium tetraborate (Li₂B₄O₇, Sigma‑Aldrich), melt the mixture in a platinum crucible using a Fusion Machine Type VAA2 (HD Elektronik), allow the fused bead to solidify, then analyse it by X‑ray fluorescence (PANalytical Axios) using GeoWSU software. Perform each measurement in duplicate.

steps.title: Digest incinerated ash for ICP‑OES (Method B)
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.2 g of the incinerated ash, add 6 mL HCl, 2 mL HNO₃ and 2 mL HF, microwave‑digest in an MLS Ethos system, complex excess HF with boric acid, dilute the digest to 50 mL with de‑ionised water (conductivity < 0.055 µS cm⁻¹), and measure Al, Ca, Fe, K, Mg, Na, P, S, Si and Ti at the following wavelengths (nm): Al 308.215, Ca 317.933, Fe 238.204, K 766.491, Mg 279.553, Na 589.592, P 213.618, S 180.669, Si 251.611, Ti 334.941 using an ICP‑OES (Varian Vista‑MPX CCD Simultaneous). Convert the elemental concentrations to the corresponding oxides (Al₂O₃, CaO, Fe₂O₃, K₂O, MgO, Na₂O, P₂O₅, SO₃, SiO₂, TiO₂). Perform each analysis in duplicate.

steps.title: Digest non‑incinerated sample (Method C)
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.2 g of the dried, non‑incinerated <0.5 mm sample, add 6 mL HCl, 2 mL HNO₃ and 2 mL HF, microwave‑digest (MLS Ethos), complex HF with boric acid, dilute to 50 mL with de‑ionised water (conductivity < 0.055 µS cm⁻¹). Measure Al, Ca, K, Mg, Na, P, S, Si and Ti by ICP‑OES under the same conditions as Method B, and measure Fe by ICP‑MS (Agilent 7500 ce). Convert all measured elements to oxides as in Method B. Perform each analysis in duplicate.

steps.title: Prepare fused bead for ICP‑OES (Method D)
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.1 g of the incinerated ash, mix with 1 g lithium metaborate (Sigma‑Aldrich), melt the mixture in a platinum crucible in a muffle furnace at 1050 °C for 20 min, cool the fused bead, then dissolve it in 80 mL of 2 mol L⁻¹ HCl while heating to 50‑60 °C and stirring with a PTFE stirring rod. Dilute the solution to a final volume of 250 mL with de‑ionised water (conductivity < 0.055 µS cm⁻¹). Measure the same set of elements as in Method B by ICP‑OES (Varian Vista‑MPX) at the listed wavelengths. Convert to oxides. The method detection limits are 0.2 wt % for Al₂O₃, CaO, Fe₂O₃, K₂O, MgO, Na₂O, TiO₂ and 0.3 wt % for P₂O₅, SO₃ and SiO₂. Perform a single measurement (no duplicate).

steps.title: Calculate recycling index (R‑Index)
steps.instruction: Determine the ash content (AC) of each sample as wt % of dry mass (DM). Identify the mass fractions (w₁…wₙ) of elementary oxides attributable to recycling (e.g., SiO₂, CaO, Fe₂O₃, etc.). Compute the R‑Index using R‑Index = AC × 100 × (w₁ + w₂ + … + wₙ) [% DM] as defined in Formula 1.

steps.title: Validate Method D accuracy and precision
steps.instruction: Assess trueness by analysing three proficiency‑testing materials (DCC 1‑3) from 2016‑2018 and comparing results to assigned values (z‑score < 2). Assess repeatability by selecting four SRF samples (Primary 21, 24, 39 and Secondary 1), performing the full Method D workflow ten times on each sample (same operator, same instruments), and recording the mean, standard deviation and relative standard deviation (RSD) for each oxide.

substeps.instruction: Measure proficiency materials 1‑3 (DCC) using the complete Method D procedure.
Calculate z‑scores: z = (Result − Assigned value)/Variance; confirm all z < 2.
For each of the four selected SRF samples, repeat the full Method D (incineration, fused‑bead preparation, dissolution, ICP‑OES) ten times.
Compute arithmetic mean, standard deviation and RSD for each oxide across the ten replicates.
